frames.narration: The alert rule watches the error ratio. A simple rule: page if it is above 1% in any single minute.
A short blip: for one minute the error ratio jumps to 5% and then goes back to normal by itself.
The simple rule fires. The engineer is woken at 3 a.m. for a problem that is already gone. After a few of these they start to ignore pages.
Better: the rule requires the error ratio to stay above the threshold for 5 minutes. The one-minute blip no longer pages anyone.
Best: the rule compares the error ratio with the SLO's budget. At 14 times the allowed rate over an hour, the budget would be gone in about two days.
A real incident now: 1.5% errors for 90 minutes. A threshold of 5% would never fire. The burn-rate rule notices that the budget is draining fast and pages the engineer, with a link to the runbook.
A slower leak, such as 0.7% errors all day, creates a ticket instead of a page. It matters, but it can wait for morning.
